paragraphs.title: The Psalm in Honor of the King

easy.explanation: The prayer uses the words “thee” and “thy,” addressing the king or anointed ruler.
easy.q: Who is being prayed for in this verse?

easy.explanation: The verse begins, “The LORD hear thee in the day of trouble.”
easy.q: What does the speaker ask the LORD to do?

easy.explanation: The verse specifically mentions “the day of trouble.”
easy.q: When does the speaker ask the LORD to hear the king?

medium.explanation: In this context, “defend” means to protect or guard the king.
medium.q: What does “defend” mean in the phrase “the name of the God of Jacob defend thee”?

answers: The name of the God of Jacob
medium.explanation: The verse asks that “the name of the God of Jacob” defend the king.
medium.q: What is connected with the king’s protection?

answers: It presents him as one who needs and receives divine help
It describes him as the enemy
It says he has no need of God
medium.explanation: The verse is a prayer asking God to hear and protect the king.
medium.q: How does this verse honor the king?

answers: From trouble to hearing and protection
challenge.explanation: The verse begins with trouble and asks for God’s hearing and defense.
challenge.q: What is the main movement of thought in the verse?

answers: It recalls the covenant God known to His people
It refers to a place of battle
challenge.explanation: The phrase identifies the LORD as the God of Jacob, the God who has cared for His people.
challenge.q: Why is the phrase “the God of Jacob” significant in this prayer?

answers: A prayer asks God to hear and protect the king in trouble
A song celebrates the king’s wealth
A report describes the enemy’s weapons
challenge.explanation: The verse is a direct prayer for the king’s help and protection.
challenge.q: Which statement best summarizes the verse?

paragraphs.title: Prayer for Divine Help and Fulfillment of the King’s Wishes

easy.explanation: The verse says, “Send thee help from the sanctuary.”
easy.q: From where does the speaker ask for help to be sent?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “Remember all thy offerings.”
easy.q: What does the speaker ask God to remember?

easy.explanation: The prayer asks God to “fulfil all thy counsel.”
easy.q: What does the speaker ask God to fulfill?

answers: Send the king away from Zion
medium.explanation: The phrase asks God to give the king strength from Zion.
medium.q: What does “strengthen thee out of Zion” mean?

medium.explanation: The verse connects the burnt sacrifice with the king’s offerings presented before God.
medium.q: What is a “burnt sacrifice” in this passage?

answers: Help, strength, remembrance, acceptance, fulfillment, and salvation
Defeat, mourning, exile, rebuilding, and rest
Crowning, feasting, traveling, singing, and sleeping
medium.explanation: The prayer asks for help and strength, remembrance of offerings, fulfillment of counsel, and salvation.
medium.q: What is the order of the main requests in these verses?

answers: The prayer presents the king’s worship before asking for divine help
The offerings are described as belonging to the enemy
The offerings replace the need for prayer
challenge.explanation: The passage mentions the king’s offerings and sacrifice within the prayer for God’s help.
challenge.q: How are the king’s offerings related to the requests for help?

answers: The prayer asks God to grant the king’s sincere wishes
The king is asking for the enemy’s plans
challenge.explanation: The phrase refers to what the king desires in his heart.
challenge.q: What does “according to thine own heart” suggest about the king’s desires?

answers: The speakers express confidence that the LORD saves His anointed
The speakers begin trusting in horses
challenge.explanation: Verse 6 says, “Now know I that the LORD saveth his anointed.”

paragraphs.title: Confidence in God’s Deliverance Against the Enemy

easy.explanation: The verse says, “Some trust in chariots, and some in horses.”
easy.q: What do some people trust in?

answers: The name of the LORD their God
easy.explanation: The people say, “we will remember the name of the LORD our God.”

answers: They are brought down and fallen
easy.explanation: The verse says, “They are brought down and fallen.”

answers: Trust in military strength versus remembering the LORD
medium.explanation: The passage contrasts trust in chariots and horses with trust in the LORD’s name.
medium.q: What is the main contrast in these verses?

answers: He saves him and hears him
medium.explanation: The passage says that the LORD saves His anointed and hears him from heaven.
medium.q: What does the LORD do for His anointed?

medium.explanation: The verse contrasts the fallen enemies with those who are “risen, and stand upright.”
medium.q: What happens to the people who remember the LORD?

answers: God’s saving power is greater than military strength
The people should trust in horses
challenge.explanation: The passage shows that reliance on the LORD prevails over reliance on weapons.
challenge.q: What conclusion follows from the contrast between chariots and the LORD’s name?

answers: The LORD has powerful ability to deliver
challenge.explanation: The phrase describes God’s powerful and saving action.
challenge.q: What does the phrase “with the saving strength of his right hand” emphasize?

answers: The enemies fall; the people rise
The enemies rise; the people fall
Both sides flee from the battle
challenge.explanation: The passage says, “They are brought down and fallen: but we are risen, and stand upright.”
challenge.q: Which pair best describes the outcome for the two sides?

easy.q: To whom is the final appeal addressed?
What does the speaker ask the LORD to do?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “let the king hear us when we call.”
easy.q: When does the speaker ask the king to hear?

answers: With a direct request for salvation and an answer
medium.explanation: The final verse is a direct plea for the LORD to save and hear His people.

answers: The people ask for salvation and for the king to hear their call
They are unrelated statements about battle
Both phrases describe the enemy’s defeat
medium.explanation: The verse joins the request for salvation with the request to be heard when calling.
medium.q: What is the relationship between “Save, LORD” and “hear us”?

answers: The people are actively crying out for help
The people are celebrating a harvest
medium.explanation: The phrase describes the people calling out in prayer.

answers: It gathers the earlier prayers into one final plea for salvation
It changes the subject to agriculture
challenge.explanation: The final verse summarizes the need for divine rescue and a gracious answer.
challenge.q: Why is this appeal effective as the conclusion of the psalm?

answers: Both ask for the king or people to be heard in a time of need
challenge.explanation: The psalm begins with a request that the LORD hear in trouble and ends with a request to hear when they call.
challenge.q: What connection exists between the beginning and ending of the psalm?

challenge.explanation: The direct command expresses an urgent plea for God’s deliverance.
challenge.q: What does the imperative “Save” reveal about the speaker’s attitude?
